notes: The wiring diagram image was not provided. The tutorial text says the matrix is powered from the Nano Matter 3V3 pin and controlled over I2C. So the four connections are 3V3→VCC, GND→GND, SDA→SDA and SCL→SCL, each through one jumper wire via the breadboard.
I assumed the Nano Matter's I2C pins are A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL), as on the standard Nano layout.

The Nano Matter straddles the breadboard centre gap. Only the pins that are used are listed as joined, and the exact column numbers are an assumption. A4, A5 and GND.1 are on the top half, 3V3 is on the bottom half. Each pin sits in a different column, so no strips are shorted.
Each jumper wire has one end in the same breadboard strip as its Nano pin, and the other end in the matrix's header pin.
The 3V3 supply is within the matrix's range, and no series resistors are needed because the matrix is a Grove module with its own drivers.
The USB-C cable plugs into the Nano Matter. This is the only power and programming link.
The Eero Thread Border Router and the Alexa app are network and software items, so they are not in the graph.
